provenance.workstream: Phase 2 carrier-cost chart: primary source search
provenance.evidence_grade_key: A official primary with table; B official primary figure reading (or text annotation on a figure); C peer-reviewed secondary; D other secondary
provenance.headline: The SIP Energy Carriers cost-comparison chart was located as slide 11 of a 2019 conference presentation by the SIP programme director (Muraki). No Cabinet Office, JST or Institute of Applied Energy table, report or brochure containing the chart or its underlying yen/Nm3 values was found. The slide gives only axis ticks and three text annotations; it states no target year, cost basis, transport distance, scale, feedstock-hydrogen cost, or scope of 'dehydrogenation'. The bar totals could NOT be read from this source in this session (the slide's chart is graphics inside a PDF that could not be rendered here).
not_found: Original SIP final report or Institute of Applied Energy cost analysis with numerical table
Currency year / JPY-USD exchange rate used for the chart
Original unit (yen per normal cubic metre of hydrogen) values
Feedstock hydrogen cost, transport distance, plant scale
Definition of 'dehydrogenation & refinement' (cracking plus purification grade)
Any cost per kg H2 of ammonia cracking plus purification in the SIP material read
Any gas-turbine efficiency or cost comparison of direct ammonia against cracked ammonia in the SIP material read

entries.quantity: Cost comparison chart of energy carriers, same bar structure (LH2, MCH, NH3 dehydrogenation, NH3 direct combustion, NH3 CH4+CCS direct combustion)
entries.value: chart present; y axis 'Hydrogen [USD/kg]' with ticks $1/kg, $2/kg, $3/kg, $4/kg; headings 'CO2-free H2 -> Carriers -> H2' and 'CH4 + CCS -> NH3'; bar labels LH2, MCH, NH3 Dehydrogenation, NH3 Direct Combustion, NH3 CH4 + CCS Direct Combustion
entries.page_or_figure: PDF page 12 of 16 (printed slide number 11), slide title 'Cost Comparison of Energy Carriers'; no source line was extracted from the text layer
entries.status: verbatim (slide text); no bar values extracted
entries.notes: Conference presentation (Ammonia = Hydrogen 2.0 Conference, Melbourne, 22 August 2019) by the SIP Energy Carriers programme director, in his capacity as Representative Director of The Green Ammonia Consortium. It is not a Cabinet Office or JST publication, so grade B is the ceiling and applies only to what the slide text states. The slide carries no assumptions.

entries.quantity: Ammonia price annotation on the cost chart (CO2-free hydrogen route, as placed beside the chart)
entries.status: verbatim (text); which bar each of the two prices belongs to is an inference from the order of the text and from the arithmetic in muraki_derived_check, not read from the graphic
entries.uncertainty: assignment of price to bar: moderate
entries.notes: Ammonia price at the point of the supply chain the chart labels, boundary (CFR import, plant gate or delivered) not stated.

entries.quantity: Ammonia price annotation on the cost chart (CH4 + CCS route)
entries.status: verbatim (text); assignment to the CH4+CCS bar inferred
entries.notes: Consistent with the 'Estimated Import Price $330 to 340/ton ($2/kg-H2)' on the previous slide (entry muraki_import_price_blue).

entries.quantity: Estimated import price of CO2-free (blue) ammonia delivered to Japan, feasibility studies for coal power plants
entries.value: 330 to 340 USD/t NH3, stated as 2 USD per kg H2
entries.unit: USD per tonne NH3; USD per kg H2
entries.page_or_figure: PDF page 11 (printed slide 10): 'Estimated Import Price $330 ~ 340/ton ($2/kg-H2); Cost comparable with renewables in Japan; Viable low carbon option for coal power'
entries.notes: Natural gas Haber-Bosch plant with CCS/EOR in Australia, US or Middle East, ammonia delivered to Japan, used for pulverised coal co-firing. This is the energy-content equivalence of ammonia used directly, expressed per kg of hydrogen contained; it does not include any dehydrogenation.

entries.quantity: Hydrogen content equivalence of the annotated ammonia prices (derived by the project, not stated in the source)
entries.unit: USD per kg H2 contained in NH3
entries.original_value_unit: computed as price / 177.6 kg H2 per tonne NH3 (3 x 1.008 / 17.031 = 17.76 wt %)
entries.page_or_figure: arithmetic on slide 10 and slide 11 text
entries.status: derived (arithmetic on verbatim values); not a reading of the chart
entries.uncertainty: exact arithmetic; the slide's own '$2/kg-H2' for 330-340 USD/t agrees (1.86-1.91 rounds to about 2)
entries.notes: The arithmetic supports the order of magnitude of the NH3 direct-combustion bars (about 2.8 USD/kg H2 for the CO2-free-hydrogen route, about 1.9 to 2.1 for the CH4+CCS route). It cannot confirm the chart's exact bar heights, nor the dehydrogenation increment, because the chart's bar values are not stated as text.

entries.quantity: Volumetric hydrogen content of the three carriers
entries.unit: kg H2 per m3 of liquid carrier
entries.original_value_unit: NH3 121 kg-H2/m3 liquid, LH2 71 kg-H2/m3, MCH 23 kg-H2/m3
entries.notes: Physical property, not a cost; included because it explains the marine-transport component.

entries.quantity: Ammonia gas-turbine demonstration results reported by SIP
entries.value: 50 kW and 300 kW turbines generated power on 100 % ammonia with NOx below 10 ppm using an ordinary SCR device; 2 MW class gas turbine stable flame and low NOx at 20 % ammonia co-fired with natural gas; commercialisation of 50 kW and 300 kW ammonia turbines planned for 2020
entries.notes: No electrical efficiency and no cost per kWh is given for direct ammonia against cracked ammonia or hydrogen in this source. The slide on a 100 MW-class advanced combined cycle shows only a block diagram (decomposition system feeding a hydrogen combustor) without numbers.

entries.value: SIP launched 2014 as a 5-year national programme under the Council for Science, Technology and Innovation, Cabinet Office; Energy Carriers programme director Shigeru Muraki (then Executive Adviser, Tokyo Gas); total budget 2014 to 2018 16.7 billion yen (150 M USD)
entries.notes: Gives the identity of the programme; implies a rate of about 111 yen per USD (16.7 bn / 150 M), derived, not stated as the chart's rate.

entries.quantity: Official JST / Cabinet Office SIP Energy Carriers programme brochures, 2015 and 2016 editions, text layer read
entries.value: no hydrogen-cost table, no USD/kg or yen/Nm3 values, no ammonia cracking cost, no turbine efficiency found
entries.uncertainty: figures embedded as images could not be inspected, so a chart without text labels cannot be excluded
entries.evidence_grade: A (as official documents; no numbers extracted)
entries.notes: The 2015 edition URL is https://www.jst.go.jp/sip/pdf/SIP_energycarriers2015.pdf. They describe the three carriers, the direct-use routes (ammonia gas turbine, fuel cells, boilers, furnaces) and the project teams. A team report https://www.jst.go.jp/sip/dl/k04/end/team4-1.pdf downloaded but its text layer was empty (scanned or image PDF); not read.

entries.quantity: Readings supplied by the orchestrator from a bar chart in course material
entries.page_or_figure: course slide; not a citable source
entries.status: figure reading, unverified against any citable source; NOT to be cited
entries.uncertainty: plus or minus 0.1 USD/kg is a plausible reading error for a stacked bar; not quantified
entries.notes: Only the NH3 direct-combustion levels have an independent arithmetic cross-check (500 USD/t gives 2.82; 335 USD/t gives 1.89 USD/kg H2, the CCS bar reading of 2.1 also contains distribution cost). LH2, MCH and the dehydrogenation increment have no check.
